description: Add a hint/rumor/lore fragment. textId is unique.
name: addHint

textId.description: Slug identifier of the hint, format [a-z0-9-]+. For references from nodes/NPCs.

source.description: Source of the hint: "NPC <name>", "A book in the monastery", "A rumor in the tavern", "An old diary". Helps the planner choose how to present it.

content.description: The hint text itself — what the players will hear/read. Direct speech or a description of the content. 1-3 sentences.

category.description: Hint category (see [AiBookHintCategory]). Hint/lore fragment category: Rum=a rumor in public places (publicly available, may be embellished); Lor=knowledge about the world/history/rules (via an expert NPC or a book); Wrn=a warning about danger (what awaits around the corner, saves the inattentive); Sec=hidden information (behind a skill check, in a cache, in a secret room); Obj=a goal/quest hook ("X needs to be done", "the roads to Y go through Z").

relatedTextIds.description: textIds of the NPCs/nodes/items/encounters the hint relates to. Helps the planner understand when it is appropriate to present it (next to this entity).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add an item/loot/artifact. textId is unique.
name: addItem

name.description: Title: "Ring of Acid Resistance", "Blueprint of a Spiked Shield", "3 Red-hot Stones", "150 gp", "Reputation at the Baron's Court".

category.description: Reward type-category (see [AiBookItemCategory]) — needed for the check "do not dump everything into gold". Item/loot category: Mon=coin (gold/silver/copper/jewels for sale, purchase flexibility); Mag=magical/mechanical item (weapon/armor/ring/consumable/scroll); Mun=ordinary mundane item (a key, a document, a tool, a blueprint, an artifact without magic); Nar=non-material reward (reputation, knowledge/secret, an NPC/faction service, access to a place, a title).

description.description: Description as a moment of the story: appearance, material, legend, feel. Not an inventory line but a trace in the fiction. 1-2 sentences.

sourceConnection.description: Binding to the source: why **this particular** item is with this NPC / in this node. "The ring came to the giant from the last city he burned", "the ritual scroll was on the cultist's person". Helps the planner present the find.

mechanics.description: D&D mechanics, if the item is magical: "+2 to hit/damage", "fire immunity for 1 minute", "can recall a 3rd-level spell". Null for ordinary items / non-material rewards.

nodeTextId.description: textId of the node where the item lies. Null if with an NPC. For non-material rewards (reputation/access) — the node where it is obtained.

npcTextId.description: textId of the NPC who holds the item / who gives the non-material reward. Null if in the node.

locationHint.description: A hint of where exactly / how it is discovered: "on the belt", "in the purse", "in a heap behind the stove", "chained to the anvil", "opens after a successful social check", "found when searching the body". Helps the planner describe the search.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a random-event table (class B events).
name: addRandomTable

name.description: Title: "Rumors at the Port", "Encounters on the Road to the Monastery", "Complications in the Fire Citadel".

category.description: Table category (see [AiBookRandomTableCategory]). Random-event table category: Rum=rumors in public places (tavern, market, guardhouse — seed the plot, draw NPC characters); Enc=random encounters on the route (another party, a wandering NPC, a creature with a motive — not a "monster for the sake of combat"); Cmp=complications (weather/environment/moral choice/obstacle — makes the road lively).

applicableNodeTextIds.description: textIds of the nodes where this table applies. Empty list = global (for example, general rumors about the BB are available everywhere).

rows.description: Table rows — at least 4, usually 6 (for a d6 roll). Each must seed the plot OR reveal the world OR telegraph a threat.

rollValue.description: Roll value: 1, 2, 3... for d6/d20. If the table has no rolls (the planner chooses) — null.

content.description: What happens/what the players hear. 1-2 sentences. Concrete — no "something strange happens".

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Record a new task for yourself as a result of self-review. Available ONLY in the SELF_REVIEW phase. After adding all tasks call transitionTo into the working phase — the frame will execute them there.
name: addTask

description.description: What exactly needs to be done

description: Mark the task as done. Use this tool after you have performed all the actions described in the task or fixed the problem found by the setter.
name: completeTask

reason.description: Optional: closing reason/comment. Required for "decision items" of the checklist (for example, refusing a book promotion): such an item is closed by a SEPARATE call with an explicit reason, not silently in a common batch.

description: Mark several tasks as done in one call. Use for going through the working phase's checklist in a row (for example, closing several 'chk-*' items) when there are no intermediate decisions between them. If an idea appears along the way — close them one by one via completeTask. REVIEW items ('rev-*', the self-check phase) are NOT closed by this tool: each requires a separate completeTask with a verdict-specific in reason, batch closing is rejected.
name: completeTasks

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo
